evidence_note: Follow-up reporting from CNA, The Business Times, The Straits Times and NTUC's FDAWU confirms Yeo Hiap Seng actually laid off 25 Singapore employees at its Senoko facility as can manufacturing shifted to Malaysia. (~25 Singapore jobs)

Standard Chartered officially announced a strategy update to cut more than 15% of corporate-function roles—over 7,000 jobs globally—as it increases AI adoption, confirmed by Business Times, CNA, BBC and others. No Singapore-specific number of cuts was disclosed; the same coverage says Singapore will hire more wealth bankers.

Follow-up coverage reports HSBC job cuts as planned/weighed, including sweeping UK wealth cuts, but does not confirm Singapore-specific layoffs or a headcount. Singapore items instead describe restructuring and AI-centre hiring.

AsiaOne reports Daiso is shuttering its Kallang Wave Mall outlet (its fourth closure this year), confirming the store closure that underpins the rumored job losses; Business Times follow-up (2026-08-22) discusses Daiso's cost pressures but no Singapore headcount was disclosed.

Follow-up coverage confirms the Plaza Singapura revamp and reports retail workers' uncertainty and some store closures, but does not confirm actual layoffs or provide a Singapore headcount. The job-cut impact therefore remains anticipated/unconfirmed rather than confirmed or denied.

Follow-up reporting confirms Crisil extended the timeline for closing its Coalition Singapore subsidiary, but it still describes the closure as anticipated rather than confirming Singapore job cuts have occurred or are underway. No headcount is provided.
Follow-up reporting confirms Yong He Eating House was set to close by end-November 2025, substantiating the earlier closure/job-impact rumor. No specific Singapore headcount was disclosed.

The 1,000 figure is a global headcount, not Singapore-specific, so no Singapore job number can be attributed.

Follow-up reporting confirms Omnicom's post-IPG job cuts are 'mostly' done, and Campaign Asia reports the group expects headcount to fall by around 15,000 by end-2026. The 15,000 figure is global, with no Singapore-specific headcount confirmed.

Headcount remains only 'hundreds' with no Singapore-specific figure.
